title: JONATHAN: THE QUALITY FRIEND
mv: Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.
mvp: “Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.” 1 Samuel 18:3 (NKJV)
assignment: Do something meaningful to appreciate the quality friends in your life this week (No mark).

b.x: Jonathan was the eldest son of Saul, the first king of Israel, from the tribe of Benjamin. His mother was Ahinoam (1 Samuel 14:50), and he had one son, Mephibosheth. Jonathan was killed alongside his father and two brothers during the battle with the Philistines on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31:2-8). His death prompted David’s heartfelt lament, known as the “Song of the Bow” (2 Samuel 1:17-27). Jonathan is remembered as one of the noblest souls who ever lived-a model of true friendship and an example of the kind of friend everyone should aspire to be or have.

Jonathan demonstrated a remarkable ability to build strong and meaningful relationships with those around him (1 Samuel 14:7; 1 Samuel 20:41). He was both courageous and physically capable, displaying athleticism and bravery in battle (1 Samuel 14:13; 2 Samuel 1:22-23). Rather than seek authority, Jonathan chose the path of service (1 Samuel 23:17). His loyalty to his father was balanced with personal conviction and the courage to act according to his beliefs. It was only once he openly expressed his anger toward Saul, and this was prompted by his father’s unjust hostility toward David (1 Samuel 20:30-34). Even then, Jonathan remained deeply loving and devoted to his father (2 Samuel 1:23). He also possessed the wisdom to keep strategic plans confidential (1 Samuel 14:1).

Jonathan’s assault on the Philistine garrison at Geba (or Gibeah) was both timely and courageous, marked by wisdom and bold faith (1 Samuel 14:1-8). He was highly skilled in archery and renowned for his prowess with the bow (2 Samuel 1:22). Fully persuaded of David’s divine destiny, Jonathan assisted him in escaping Saul’s attempts on his life and worked persistently to calm his father’s hostility toward David, achieving some measure of success (1Samuel 19:4-7; 20:30-33).

Jonathan entered into a covenant of loyalty with David and remained faithful to it, even when his father, King Saul, turned against David (1 Samuel 18:3; 20:30-35). Through his son Mephibosheth, Jonathan’s lineage endured for several generations, producing notable warriors who, like their forefather, were distinguished for their skill with the bow (1 Chronicles 8:40).

i: Jonathan loved David as himself (1 Samuel 18:1-4).
He established trust and reliability by consistently warning David about Saul’s evil intentions, even at the risk of his own life (1 Samuel 20:1-23, 32-33).
Their friendship was mutually strengthened, showing that genuine friendships build faith and shape character (Proverbs 27:17).
Jonathan exemplified wholehearted obedience to God by honouring His chosen king, even when it cost him personally, including the loss of his claim to the throne-a powerful lesson for believers today.
Selflessness stands out as the defining mark of true and enduring friendship.

b.x: Jonathan’s devotion to his friend David is a virtue lacking in many relationships today.

i: What are the achievements of Jonathan?
Enumerate four lessons you have learned from his life.
